sections.h2: Who sends and who values a property tax bill in Madison County, NC?
sections.html:
Two county offices share the work: the tax assessor values and lists property, and the Board of Commissioners sets the rate that turns that value into a bill. Madison County, North Carolina has its tax administration office at 5707 Highway 25/70, Room 25, in Marshall, open Monday through Friday from 8:00am to 5:00pm. The main number is 828-649-0734.

The county's own assessor page says the assessor does not raise or lower taxes. Rates come from the commissioners, and collection happens through the tax collector. If you want to challenge a bill, the place to start is the value on it, because a higher bill by itself is not a valid ground for an appeal, according to the county's formal appeal form.

Madison County covers 449.62 square miles of land, per the Census Bureau's 2020 figures. About 47.1 people live on each square mile, so parcels range from town lots in Marshall to large hillside tracts. That spread is one reason valuation questions come up so often for sellers here.

sections.h2: What are the Madison County property tax rates?
sections.html:
The county rate on the posted sheet is 0.36 per $100 of value for all townships, with extra charges for the fire district and town where the parcel sits. The sheet is headed 2024-2025, so ask tax administration for the rate sheet that matches the bill you are looking at.

sections.h2: How is a Madison County home valued, and how often?
sections.html:
The assessor appraises on the cost, income and market approaches and blends them into one assessed value. North Carolina requires every county to reappraise real property at least every eight years, and Madison County contracts an outside appraisal firm to help with that work.

Real property stays on the roll year to year, so you do not re-list a house each January. Personal property is different. Single-wide mobile homes, boats, farm machinery, unlicensed campers and business equipment must be listed every year during the January 1 to 31 listing period.

The assessor's office also keeps the ownership changes and the parcel maps, and the county runs a GIS system with boundary lines and aerial photos. If you plan to sell, pull the parcel on the county's property card search first and check the acreage, the building description and the owner name. A wrong square footage or a missing outbuilding is easier to fix before a buyer's attorney finds it.

sections.h2: When are Madison County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Taxes are due September 1 and are payable at face value through January 5. Interest starts on January 6 under state law.

  • Listing period for personal property: January 1 through January 31, with extensions possible under state law.
  • Bills due: September 1 of the fiscal year they are levied for.
  • Interest: 2 percent from January 6, then three-fourths of one percent a month starting February 1.
  • Mailed payments count as paid on the postmark date.

A county or town may also adopt an early-payment discount by resolution, so ask the collector whether one applies to your bill. For payment options, call 828-649-0734 or use the online payment link on the tax administration page.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Madison County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the assessor's formal appeal form, mailed to the Madison County Assessor's Office, 5707 US 25/70, Suite 3 Box 4, Marshall, NC 28753. The 2026 form asks for your opinion of fair market value as of January 1, 2024.

It also asks when you bought, what you paid, whether the house was inherited or bought from a family member, and whether an independent appraisal exists. If the property is listed for sale, you must give the asking price and attach the listing contract. Income property needs three years of income and expense figures. Someone who does not own the parcel must file a notarized power of attorney approved by the assessor.

If the assessor does not resolve it, the next step is the county board of equalization and review, which is the Board of Commissioners unless a separate board exists. It first meets between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May. You ask for a hearing in writing or in person before it adjourns. A further appeal goes to the Property Tax Commission within 30 days after the board mails its decision.

sections.h2: What property tax relief exists for Madison County owners?
sections.html:
North Carolina offers three programs, and an owner can use only one of them. Madison County's assessor page points owners to the elderly and disabled exclusion, the agricultural or forestry land use program, and property tax exemptions.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50 percent of appraised value is excluded. You must be 65 or totally and permanently disabled and have income under the limit, which NCDOR lists as $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value is excluded, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: tax is limited to 4 percent of income, or 5 percent if income is above the limit and up to 150 percent of it, which NCDOR prints as $58,200 for 2026. You need five years of ownership and occupancy.

File on Form AV-9 with the county assessor, not the state. It should go in during the listing period, but the county must accept it through June 1. The circuit breaker needs a fresh application every year. Sources: NCDOR Form AV-9 and G.S. 105-277.1B.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid or deferred tax when a Madison County house sells?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax follows the parcel, not the owner. The lien attaches on the date property is listed under G.S. 105-285, with penalties, interest and costs, so a buyer's attorney will want the bill paid or credited at closing.

If you are on the circuit breaker, the deferred amount for the three prior fiscal years becomes due when you transfer the home, die, or stop living in it. Madison County's tax administration page asks attorneys and paralegals for 10 days' notice to create deferred tax bills, so build that into your closing timeline.

If taxes stay unpaid, the county can foreclose by court action and sell at auction at the courthouse door. Madison County's tax administration page has a tax foreclosure sales link. A sale in fee simple clears most liens, and a person redeeming before confirmation pays the taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

sections.h2: What does selling a Madison County house with tax due look like?
sections.html:
Madison County had an estimated 22,553 residents on July 1, 2025, and the Census Bureau counts 8,342 households and 25.3 percent of residents age 65 or older. Older owners often hold land that has stayed in a family for decades, and that can mean back taxes, unlisted outbuildings or unclear heirs.

  • Ask the tax office for a current statement on each parcel, including any deferred amounts.
  • Confirm the owner name on the tax record matches the deed.
  • Check whether a relief program or land use classification is on the parcel before a buyer takes it over.
  • Order any survey before you list if acreage is uncertain.

A cash buyer can close around a tax balance, since the amount owed comes out of the sale proceeds and the rest goes to you. That can help when repairs, probate or a missed bill have made a regular listing hard.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Madison County, NC property tax bill?
faqs.a: Call Madison County Tax Administration at 828-649-0734. The office is at 5707 Highway 25/70, Room 25, Marshall, and it is open Monday through Friday from 8:00am to 5:00pm.

faqs.q: What is the Madison County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The posted sheet headed 2024-2025 shows 0.36 per $100 of value for the county, plus a fire district rate and a town rate where one applies. Marshall is printed at 0.355, Mars Hill at 0.47 and Hot Springs at 0.45.

faqs.q: Is a higher tax bill a reason to appeal in Madison County?
faqs.a: No. The county's formal appeal form says an increase in the bill is not a valid reason. An appeal has to argue that the assessed fair market value is wrong, and the form asks for your own value opinion and supporting facts.

faqs.q: When does interest start on Madison County property tax?
faqs.a: Interest starts on January 6 after the September 1 due date, at 2 percent. From February 1 it runs three-fourths of one percent a month until the bill is paid.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Madison County house if the property tax is unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax is a lien on the parcel, so it is paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the tax office for a payoff figure first, and give the office extra time if you have a deferred circuit breaker bill.
